title: Unify eval-runner contracts with dataset signature metadata and model-version pinning
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
We need a robust bridge between dataset signatures (schema, tokenization assumptions, deterministic sampler seed) and eval runners so that published performance profiles are reproducible and safely pin to model+artifact variants. Current harness outputs profiles with free-form metadata which leads to drifting comparisons and flaky rollouts when minor dataset or prompt changes occur.

Goals:
- Define a strict 'dataset_signature' contract consumed by eval runners that includes tokenizer id, canonical prompt ids, sampling seed, and canonical train/val split hash.
- Implement a reconciliation CLI that verifies model_version pin + dataset_signature before profile publish; fail CI when mismatches appear.
- Emit a normalized profile artifact (JSONL + manifest) containing: model_version, quantization_profile, perf_metrics, dataset_signature, seed, runtime config, and provenance links.
- Add guardrails to profile publisher so automatic rollouts only use profiles with matching signatures or explicit opt-in.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Strict signatures improve reproducibility but increase friction for iterative prompt edits. To mitigate, the reconciliation tool supports a 'semantic-diff' mode that surfaces small prompt edits and allows PM/Research to approve a signature bump via console.
- We will canonicalize tokenizer representation to a stable tokenizer_id (vocab hash + tokenizer type) rather than raw tokenizer file path to avoid environment-specific drift.
- We keep eval runners backward-compatible by supporting a compatibility layer: if an incoming profile has an older signature version, the runner will map fields and emit a deprecation warning for 3 cycles.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Spec: dataset_signature schema + canonical manifest (confluence doc) — complete (links below).
2) Eval-runner contract updates (API + CLI) — in progress (PR opened).
3) Reconciliation CLI + CI gating rule — wiring + unit tests pending.
4) Profile publisher changes (manifest validation + staging bucket) — ready for integration test.
5) Console UX: approval workflow for signature bumps — mild UX work with PM.

Progress updates:
- 2026-03-02: Initial spec posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONB/Dataset+Signature+Spec (doc contains examples and schema).
- 2026-03-04: Prototype eval-runner change implemented; added tokenizer_id normalization and sampling-seed parameter. Local runs show reproducible token-latency within 1% across 3 invocations. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/4128
- 2026-03-07: Integration run with lm-model-x@v2026-02-28 produced profile artifact; identified missing provenance for quantization profile -> added quantization_profile_id field to manifest.
- 2026-03-10: Reconciliation CLI core implemented (python); failing cases detected in old archived profiles (12% of artifacts) where split-hash missing. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/pull/221
- 2026-03-12: Design review with PM and Research; agreed to add 'semantic-diff' approval flow and add a size threshold where tiny prompt edits (<=3 token edit distance) are auto-allowed for non-SLA profiles.

Acceptance criteria:
- Eval runners validate incoming dataset_signature and refuse runs when required fields missing (tokenizer_id, split_hash, seed).
- Reconciliation CLI returns non-zero exit in CI when model_version != pinned_version or when signature changed without approval.
- Published profile artifacts contain manifest with at least the required fields and a stable manifest schema version.
- E2E test reproduces perf numbers within historical tolerance (latency +-5%, throughput +-7%) for pinned model+signature combinations on staging hardware.

Testing & safety:
- Added unit tests for tokenizer_id normalization and split_hash computation.
- Added golden prompt-set tests: harness will run canonical prompt ids and compare outputs to stored token-level hashes to detect drift.
- CI gating: reconciliation CLI will run on profile publish pipeline. Non-matching signatures require manual approval with audit trail.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: Deploy eval-runner contract + publisher validation to staging; run nightly verification against 100 archived profiles and flag mismatches (2 weeks).
- Stage 2: Enable CI gating for all new profile publishes; prevent auto-rollout if signature does not match (1 week).
- Stage 3: After confidence window and PM approval UX in console, enable for production publish.

Links & artifacts:
- Spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONB/Dataset+Signature+Spec
- Harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/4128
- Tools PR (reconciliation CLI): https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/pull/221
- Example profile artifact (staging): gs://redwood-profiles/staging/lm-model-x_v2026-02-28/manifest.json

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we want signature-aware rollbacks that automatically search for the most recent compatible profile when a signature mismatch occurs? (Engineering + Product decision)
- Should we store prompt-edit diffs in the profile manifest or keep diffs in a separate prompt registry to avoid large manifests?

Owner notes:
- I will continue to iterate on the reconciliation CLI test suite this cycle. Blocking items: need runtime team to expose tokenizer_id on the inference side for the canonicalizer (ticket assigned to infra).

QA checklist (for PR reviewers):
- Confirm manifest schema v1/v2 compatibility tests included.
- Ensure reconciliation CLI returns clear error codes for CI automation.
- Confirm that console approval writes an audit line with user, timestamp and diff summary.
